Condition review: good shape; support cables need maintenance and the platform needs repair; staffed as needed

corrections.why: The Register describes a 42-foot tower with an open 6 by 6 foot cab on a well casing, not a bare platform.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register describes an open 6 by 6 foot cab; the Forest Lookouts summary describes a covered platform. The story reports the difference rather than choosing one.

The Register calls the lookout Cedar Tree Lookout. The park's Cedar Tree Tower is a separate ancient site near the four-way intersection on Chapin Mesa; the sources do not say the lookout takes its name from it.

notes_for_editor: Access, visiting and rental status are not in any source read, so no access or visit keys are set. Staffing is from the 2019 Register review only; no current staffing source. No fire history found. Record kind 'platform' is proposed as 'tower with open cab'. The NPS page is for an ancient tower with a similar name and does not mention this lookout. Park Point Lookout, the park's other lookout, was not researched. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story no longer calls the Forest Lookouts summary 'earlier' (its date is not given) and says towers were mainly built in the Classic period, rather than 'around' those dates.
